rows.label: Take the required introductory course, Introduction to American Studies
Take one 4000-level American Studies seminar
rows.note: The page does not say which 4000-level courses are seminars. The board counts AMST-coded courses numbered 4000-4999 of at least 3 credits, leaving out the honors tutorials; the confirm row below covers the seminar format. Only AMST-coded courses count here so the discipline cap on the other courses stays easy to check.

rows.label: Take three more American Studies courses at the 2000 level or above (pre-1900, diversity and an elective)
rows.note: Five courses minus the intro and the seminar leaves three, all 2000+ (the one allowed course below 2000 is the intro). Cross-listed courses count, but at most two may carry a non-AMST code (stricter than the two-per-discipline cap, whose home disciplines the board cannot see). Courses under 3 credits and honors tutorials are left out so the minor reaches 15 credits.

rows.label: One of your courses must be a pre-1900 course; confirm which one qualifies
rows.note: The page gives no list or definition of pre-1900 courses, so the board cannot check it.

rows.label: One of your courses must be an American diversity course (social justice or inequality: race, class, gender, sexuality); confirm which one qualifies
rows.note: The page gives no list of diversity courses, so the board cannot check it.

rows.label: Confirm that your 4000-level American Studies course is a seminar
rows.note: The page does not list which 4000-level courses are seminars.

rows.label: Confirm that no more than two of your courses come from any one discipline or field
rows.note: The board cannot see each cross-listed course's home discipline. It already holds non-AMST-coded courses to two in total, which is stricter than the page.

rows.label: Every course finished with a grade of C or better; at most one course S/U, and AMST 1101 taken for a letter grade
File the Intent to Declare AMST Minor form, by your second-to-last semester
Confirm completion with the AMST Undergraduate Coordinator by the middle of your last semester
